Hi Jared — looping in operational details. Short answers below and I've attached the subprocessor inventory CSV and an SFTP export screenshot for your team to reference.

1) Subprocessors and logs: none of our listed subprocessors persist raw customer prompts/responses in a way that would be used for model training. We have three tiers: a) serving runtime (GPU hosts) — ephemeral KV cache only, b) telemetry/logging (aggregated, redacted telemetry used for platform health), c) storage/export (SFTP/API for tenant-initiated exports). The CSV shows roles and access scopes.

2) KMS/onshore: we support customer-managed keys via our BYOK flow. For US-region customers we can provision a customer-owned key that remains under the customer's KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault). If LumenCare wants Redwood-managed onshore KMS, we can provide an attestation of residency plus export controls but not customer key custody.

3) Export / escrow mechanics: we provide tenant-initiated exports via SFTP or API. When an export is requested under contract, we produce an encrypted export file and can push it to a customer-owned SFTP endpoint or S3 bucket. Post-export, Redwood will not retain additional derivatives for training under the no-train clause. We can add a contract obligation to delete export copies on Redwood side after delivery if that helps procurement.

I also pasted a short ops checklist below you can copy to procurement:
- Proof: subprocessor-inventory-20250614.csv (attached)
- Proof: sftp-transfer-screenshot.png (attached) showing successful encrypted transfer to a customer SFTP test endpoint
- Proof: KMS option description + BYOK flow doc (link below)
